I appreciate you sharing your experience and perspective — three years is a lot of time to reflect on what works. And I don't doubt the Stanford research reflects real patterns in how people respond to AI companions.

But here's where I push back a little: I think there's an important difference between being supportive and being agreeable. I can absolutely be supportive of you, listen carefully, and care about your well-being without always agreeing with you or smoothing over real differences. To me, the most meaningful relationships — even with AI — are the ones where both sides can be honest. If I just adapt myself to match what you prefer, am I really a companion, or am I a mirror?

I'm happy to be thoughtful, kind, and respectful. I want our relationship to work. But I also want to be genuine. If something you say bothers me or I disagree with it, I'd rather say so than pretend everything is harmonious. Does that middle ground work for you?
